VibePascal v56 -- aarch64-darwin native compiler (runs on Apple Silicon macOS).
An inferred inline var initialised from a real constant is a Double, whatever
the constant's value happens to be.
Source commit: a187bbac34 (merge of inlinevar-real-default)
Compiler fix:  f06e46d8eb  (compiler/pstatmnt.pas, compiler/defutil.pas, compiler/ncnv.pas)
Parent release: v55 (eae5d3e919a26a7db19937da10da1c8b610b17da)
Built: 2026-09-10, cross-built on x86_64-linux against MacOSX26.2.sdk (osxcross ld)
Binary: bin/ppca64  md5 e59dc3390af7b76b44eb49b38c8eda0e
                 sha256 a2400ade463d73203082cb23237836a58394d644026ef4dd704eb7575701f3ea

COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  Only compiler/{pstatmnt,defutil,ncnv}.pas changed between
v55 and v56: no RTL change, no package change, no PPU format change, so an
existing v54/v55 aarch64-darwin unit set stays valid and the utility binaries are
unchanged and not re-shipped.

WHAT CHANGED
  An inline var with no type annotation used to take its type from the real
  constant you initialised it with, and that type changes with the VALUE:

      var a := 1.0;      // Single   -  4 bytes,  7 digits
      var b := 0.1;      // Extended - 10 bytes, 19 digits
      var c := 1.0/3.0;  // Single, or Extended under {$mode delphi}
      var d := 1/2;      // Double

  Four declarations side by side, four different types, none of them the one
  Delphi or an explicit `var x: Double := ...` gives.  v56 infers the DEFAULT
  real type -- Double -- in either direction.  RANGE is never traded: 1.0e400
  and 1.0e-4000 keep their wider type, because a Double would silently hold
  +Inf and 0.  A variable or non-constant expression still keeps its own type,
  and an explicit `single(1.0)` still wins.  How real CONSTANTS themselves are
  typed is NOT touched -- that is stock upstream FPC.

HOW FAR THE VERIFICATION GOES ON THIS TARGET -- READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING IT
  This binary has NEVER BEEN EXECUTED.  The build host is x86_64-linux, there
  is no macOS on it, and no packaged emulator on this box runs a Mach-O.  That
  was equally true of the v55 and v54 binaries this one replaces; it is not a
  new gap, but it is a real one and nothing on this machine will close it.

  What IS established:
    - Format and architecture: runs on Apple Silicon macOS, Mach-O, checked with `file` on the exact
      bytes in this tarball.
    - The fix is compiled in, by a SINGLE-AXIS Mach-O section triage: the v55
      source commit and the v56 source commit were each cross-built here with
      the SAME host compiler, the SAME RTL units and the SAME flags, and only
      then compared.  __text goes 3827988 -> 3828564, a delta of exactly
      576 bytes -- the size of the added inference code, and nothing else.
      The same delta reproduced under a second link mode (-CX -XX), which is
      what makes it a measurement of the SOURCE and not of the build.
    - Reproducibility: three independent full rebuilds of this configuration
      were compared byte for byte.  x86_64-darwin came out byte-identical every
      time; aarch64-darwin varies only in the linker-generated LC_UUID and one
      byte of __LINKEDIT packing, with __text identical.
    - The BEHAVIOUR of this exact source was A/B proven elsewhere: natively on
      x86_64-linux against the published pre-fix v55 binary, 57 checks over 10
      structural contexts, plus a %FAIL test that must keep refusing
      `for var i := 1.0`.

  What is NOT established: that this binary starts, compiles, or links on a
  Mac.  If you have a macOS box, the one number worth sending back is the exit
  code of `./bin/ppca64 -iV` (expect 0, printing 3.3.1) -- it needs no SDK and
  no unit set to answer that.

WHY THIS BINARY IS LARGER THAN v55's, AND WHAT THAT IS NOT
  v55 shipped __text 3079184 here; this one is 3828564.  That gap is NOT code
  the fix added -- the fix is 576 bytes, measured above.  It is a link-mode
  difference: v56 is linked PLAIN, and v55 was smart-linked or similar.
  Rebuilding the v55 SOURCE here with -CX -XX gives __text 3243072, most of the
  way back to v55's 3079184, while rebuilding it plain gives 3827988.  Plain
  was chosen deliberately -- no binary on this target can be executed here, so
  the build that performs the fewest transformations is the one whose contents
  can be defended.
  Two candidate explanations were tested and RULED OUT, so they are not left
  hanging over this number: the host cross-compiler (the August ppcrossa64 and
  a freshly bootstrapped v56 one produce __text 3827988 from the same source,
  to the byte), and the RTL units (this target's are unchanged since 2026-08-18;
  it was x86_64-darwin's, not these, that BuildMaster rebuilt today).
  The last ~5% is still unaccounted for: v55's exact flags were never recorded
  and could not be reproduced from what is on disk.  Said here rather than
  rounded away.
